attachments.origin_landmark: inferior cartilage of the pharyngotympanic (Eustachian) tube
attachments.insertion_landmark: blends with palatopharyngeus in the pharyngeal wall

actions: opens the pharyngotympanic tube during swallowing

functional_compartments.name: Single fiber population
functional_compartments.function_note: Raises the salpingopharyngeal fold. Its tubal action is part of why swallowing equalises middle ear pressure.
functional_compartments.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Not an ultrasound-guided technique -- described only as part of a combined paratubal-muscle injection (with tensor veli palatini and levator veli palatini) for patulous eustachian tube/autophonia, on the hypothesis that abnormal activity of these three muscles keeps the tube abnormally patent. The source does not give salpingopharyngeus its own separate landmark, dose, or approach distinct from the group injection; salpingopharyngeus runs within the salpingopharyngeal fold, deep in the nasopharynx, so any direct injection would need an endoscopic/transnasal route rather than the transoral route used for tensor veli palatini.
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Diagnosis and treatment response for the target condition (autophonia from a patulous eustachian tube) are confirmed with posterior rhinoscopy/nasopharyngoscopy and impedance audiometry/tympanometry rather than by EMG of this specific muscle.
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Evidence is thin and indirect: salpingopharyngeus is named as one of three co-injected paratubal muscles in a single case report of BoNT for autophonia, with symptom relief lasting about 9 months, rather than being independently studied or dosed. No dedicated salpingopharyngeus-specific technique was found; this is reported as a group-injection component, not a worked-out muscle-specific approach.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Olthoff A, Laskawi R, Kruse E, 'Successful treatment of autophonia with botulinum toxin: case report', Ann Otol Rhinol Laryngol 116(8):594-598 (2007), doi:10.1177/000348940711600807 -- retrieved via PubMed.
